''L'En-Avant''{{Cite web|url=https://footnickname.wordpress.com/2022/06/05/774-en-avant-de-guingamp-en-avant/|title=#774 – En Avant de Guingamp : En Avant|date=5 June 2022|language=fr|publisher=Footnickname|access-date=1 September 2022|archive-date=20 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920171605/https://footnickname.wordpress.com/2022/06/05/774-en-avant-de-guingamp-en-avant/|url-status=live}} | short name = EAG | founded = {{Start date and age|df=yes|1912}} | stadium = [[Stade de Roudourou]] | capacity = 19,060 | chairman = Frédéric Legrand | chrtitle = President | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Sylvain Ripoll]] | league = {{French football updater|Guingamp}} | season = {{French football updater|Guingamp2}} | position = {{French football updater|Guingamp3}} | website = {{URL|https://www.eaguingamp.com|eaguingamp.com}} | current = 2023–24 En Avant Guingamp season | pattern_la1 = _guingamp2526h | pattern_b1 = _guingamp2526h | pattern_ra1 = _guingamp2526h | pattern_sh1 = _guingamp2526h | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = FF0000 | body1 = FF0000 | rightarm1 = FF0000 | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = FF0000 | pattern_la2 = _guingamp2526a | pattern_b2 = _guingamp2526a | pattern_ra2 = _guingamp2526a | pattern_sh2 = _guingamp2526a | pattern_so2 = | leftarm2 = FFFFFF | body2 = FFFFFF | rightarm2 = FFFFFF | shorts2 = FFFFFF | socks2 = FFFFFF | pattern_la3 = _guingamp2526t | pattern_b3 = _guingamp2526t | pattern_ra3 = _guingamp2526t | pattern_sh3 = _guingamp2526t | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = 247D6F | body3 = F1ECE6 | rightarm3 = 247D6F | shorts3 = 247D6F | socks3 = F1ECE6 }} '''En avant de Guingamp''' ({{Langx|br|War-raok Gwengamp}}, {{langx|en|Forward Guingamp}}), commonly referred to as '''EA Guingamp''', '''EAG''', or simply '''Guingamp''' ({{IPA|fr|ɡɛ̃ɡɑ̃|lang}}), is a French professional [[Football in France|football]] club based in the [[Communes of France|commune]] of [[Guingamp]], in France's [[Brittany]] region. The club was founded in 1912 and play in [[Ligue 2]], the second tier of [[Football in France|French football]]. The club has appeared in the [[Ligue 1]], the top flight of French football, for 13 seasons, and is known for its relative success given Guingamp's small population of only 7,000 people. Guingamp are one of only two clubs who have won the [[Coupe de France]] while not being in the first division, doing so in 2009, by defeating [[Stade Rennais FC|Rennes]], 2–1. They won the same competition again in 2014, this time in the top flight, with a victory against Rennes, 2–0."}}
